content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To clean a coil, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Disconnect the main power supply to the unit (5 minutes)
Step 2. Apply a neutralizer to the metal surfaces (10 minutes)
Step 3. Perform a final high-pressure rinse (15 minutes)
Step 4. Reattach the protective outer grille (20 minutes)
Step 5. Inspect the surrounding drainage area (10 minutes)
Step 6. Mix the concentrated cleaning solution (5 minutes)
Step 7. Clear away large debris and leaves from the base (15 minutes)
Step 8. Check the fins for any structural damage (10 minutes)
Step 9. Apply a corrosion inhibitor spray (15 minutes)
Step 10. Document the initial condition of the unit (5 minutes)
Step 11. Test the pH levels of the runoff water (5 minutes)
Step 12. Set up the industrial vacuum system (10 minutes)
Step 13. Remove the access panels (15 minutes)
Step 14. Scrub the stubborn deposits with a soft brush (20 minutes)
Step 15. Lubricate the fan motor bearings (10 minutes)
Step 16. Wipe down the interior housing (15 minutes)
Step 17. Locate the coil manufacturer specifications (10 minutes)
Step 18. Straighten bent fins with a fin comb (30 minutes)
Step 19. Identify the specific type of buildup (dust vs. grease) (5 minutes)
Step 20. Clean the condensate drain pan (20 minutes)
Step 21. Reinstall the fan assembly (25 minutes)
Step 22. Verify all electrical connections are dry (10 minutes)
Step 23. Protect the electrical components with plastic (10 minutes)
Step 24. Prepare the water hose and spray nozzle (5 minutes)
Step 25. Apply a second coat of coil brightener (15 minutes)
Step 26. Clean the workspace around the unit (15 minutes)
Step 27. Replace worn-out mounting bolts (10 minutes)
Step 28. Take "before" photos of the coil (5 minutes)
Step 29. Vacuum the loose dust from the surface (20 minutes)
Step 30. Remove the internal fan blade (15 minutes)
Step 31. Gather the required safety equipment (10 minutes)
Step 32. Measure the airflow through the coil (10 minutes)
Step 33. Flush the drain line with hot water (15 minutes)
Step 34. Soak the coil in the primary cleaning agent (30 minutes)
Step 35. Inspect the refrigerant line insulation (10 minutes)
Step 36. Check for signs of refrigerant leaks (20 minutes)
Step 37. Clean the fan blades individually (20 minutes)
Step 38. Allow the unit to air dry completely (2 hours)
Step 39. Sanitize the air intake area (15 minutes)
Step 40. Inspect the mounting pad for leveling (15 minutes)
Step 41. Put on protective gloves and goggles (5 minutes)
Step 42. Organize the tool kit (10 minutes)
Step 43. Position the work lights for better visibility (5 minutes)
Step 44. Log the cleaning chemicals used (5 minutes)
Step 45. Read the chemical safety data sheets (10 minutes)
Step 46. Replace the air filters (10 minutes)
Step 47. Dispose of used cleaning rags (5 minutes)
Step 48. Check the tension of the drive belt (10 minutes)
Step 49. Apply a protective wax to the exterior cabinet (20 minutes)
Step 50. Prepare the degreasing solution (10 minutes)
Step 51. Survey the site for hazards (10 minutes)
Step 52. Pre-rinse the coil with clean water (10 minutes)
Step 53. Check the condition of the gasket seals (10 minutes)
Step 54. Rinse the cleaning solution off the coil (20 minutes)
Step 55. Evaluate the coil for deep-seated oxidation (15 minutes)
Step 56. Test the emergency shut-off switch (5 minutes)
Step 57. Secure the perimeter with caution tape (10 minutes)
Step 58. Secure the access panels back in place (15 minutes)
Step 59. Inspect the electrical conduit for cracks (15 minutes)
Step 60. Brush the exterior fins (15 minutes)
Step 61. Spray a mold inhibitor on the coil (15 minutes)
Step 62. Calibrate the temperature sensors (20 minutes)
Step 63. Remove any old service stickers (5 minutes)
Step 64. Check the fan motor mounting brackets (10 minutes)
Step 65. Clean the secondary drain pan (15 minutes)
Step 66. Treat the coil with an anti-microbial coating (20 minutes)
Step 67. Inspect the wiring harnesses (15 minutes)
Step 68. Verify the presence of a drip leg (5 minutes)
Step 69. Check the weather forecast for rain (5 minutes)
Step 70. Degrease the fan motor housing (20 minutes)
Step 71. Perform a leak test on the joints (15 minutes)
Step 72. Label the power disconnect (5 minutes)
Step 73. Inspect the contactor for pitting (10 minutes)
Step 74. Check the capacitors for bulging (10 minutes)
Step 75. Inventory the spare parts (15 minutes)
Step 76. Check the service manual for torque specs (15 minutes)
Step 77. Inspect the thermostat wiring (10 minutes)
Step 78. Clear the primary drain line blockage (20 minutes)
Step 79. Take "after" photos of the coil (5 minutes)
Step 80. Unpack the cleaning supplies (5 minutes)
Step 81. Wipe the fan motor blades (10 minutes)
Step 82. Restore power to the unit (5 minutes)
Step 83. Inspect the evaporator coil for frost (15 minutes)
Step 84. Check the compressor mounting (10 minutes)
Step 85. Verify the grounding wire connection (10 minutes)
Step 86. Check the refrigerant pressure (15 minutes)
Step 87. Inspect the thermal expansion valve (10 minutes)
Step 88. Check the isolation dampeners (10 minutes)
Step 89. Test the system operation in cooling mode (20 minutes)
Step 90. Remove the vacuum equipment (10 minutes)
